title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Internet of Things Computing: A Systematic Survey
venue: ACM Proceedings (venue not fully reported in text)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the rapidly growing body of work on generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) for Internet of Things (IoT) computing and argues that the literature is fragmented across many narrow applications. The authors aim to provide a holistic survey of the opportunities, challenges, and implications of combining GenAI with IoT, rather than focusing on a single use case or vertical domain.

The paper is a systematic literature review conducted according to PRISMA. It searches major digital libraries and screenes studies from 2020 to March 2025, ultimately analyzing 74 eligible records. The review organizes prior work using a tripartite IoT framework—Internet-oriented, object-oriented, and semantic-oriented perspectives—and further maps studies to categories of generative models such as auto-regressive models, flow-based models, variational auto-encoders, energy-based models, diffusion models, and GANs. It also compares applications, model choices, and recurring technical constraints such as resource limitations, interoperability, data quality, and privacy/security.

Because the paper is a survey rather than an intervention study, it does not involve a participant population such as students or teachers. Its context is broad cross-domain IoT computing, with examples drawn from networking, edge intelligence, healthcare, smart cities, and security. The authors conclude that GenAI can support synthetic data generation, uncertainty handling, optimization, and human-machine interaction in IoT, but practical deployment is constrained by computational cost, scalability, training instability, and the need for better domain-specific datasets and robust integration frameworks.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative artificial intelligence systems in general, including generative models and LLMs, used to create or synthesize outputs from data.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper is a systematic survey of generative artificial intelligence for Internet of Things (IoT) computing. It does not study a single educational AI product or a K-12 coaching tool; instead it reviews generative model families and their roles in IoT contexts.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic survey, not an empirical evaluation of an AI tool in K-12 education. It synthesizes prior literature across IoT generative modeling and reports no direct study outcomes for a specific tool.
impact_tier_rationale: No student, teacher, or coaching outcome is measured, and no effect sizes or intervention impacts are reported. The paper is outside the requested K–12 instructional coaching/lesson-feedback use case.
